questions.q: Parking space requirements for Private Elementary, Secondary or Vocational School
questions.n: Private primary and secondary schools require one slot for every five classrooms to accommodate staff and parents.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Public Colleges and Universities
questions.n: Public higher education institutions are mandated to provide one slot for every five classrooms.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Private Colleges and Universities
questions.n: Private universities have the highest parking density requirement among educational facilities at 1:3.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Private Mental Hospital, Sanitaria & Asylums.
questions.n: Institutional facilities like asylums have a lower parking demand of 1 slot per 25 beds.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Public Hospitals
questions.n: Public hospitals require a 1:25 bed ratio plus specific slots for public transport (jeeps) and logistics (articulated truck).

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Private Hospitals
questions.n: Private hospitals require more parking per bed (1:12) along with the standard jeepney and articulated truck slots.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Nursing Homes, Ambulatory, orphanages and the likes.
questions.n: These residential care facilities follow the same 1:12 bed ratio as private hospitals.

questions.q: Average Car perpendicular & diagonal parking measurement.
questions.n: The standard size for a perpendicular or diagonal car slot is 2.50 meters wide by 5.00 meters long.

questions.q: Average Car parallel parking measurement.
questions.n: Parallel parking slots are narrower (2.15m) but longer (6.00m) to facilitate side-entry maneuvering.

questions.q: Jeepney parking measurement.
questions.n: The standard size for a jeepney slot is 3.00 meters wide by 9.00 meters long.

questions.q: Bus/Truck parking measurement.
questions.n: Standard buses and trucks require a slot measuring 3.60 meters by 12.00 meters.

questions.q: Articulated Truck parking measurement. (10 or 12 wheeler trucks)
questions.n: Articulated trucks require the same 3.60m width but a significantly longer 18.00m length.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Terminals, Inter-modals, Depots and the likes.
questions.n: Transport terminals must provide one slot for every 500 square meters of gross floor area.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Neighborhood Shopping Center/Supermarkets
questions.n: Supermarkets and local shopping centers must provide 1 slot per 100 square meters of GFA.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Restaurants and Fast food, Bars or Beerhouses.
questions.n: Due to high turnover and customer density, restaurants require 1 slot per 30 square meters.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Theater Restaurants and Night Clubs.
questions.n: Night clubs and theater restaurants have the highest parking density requirement at 1:20.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Columbarium
questions.n: The terminology used in the code for columbarium parking is '1 per Compartment Niche'.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Breweries, Mills and other Industrial Buildings
o: 1 car per 2000 sqm.; 1 bus per 200 workers
1 car per 1000 sqm.; 2 buses per 100 workers
1 car per 500 sqm.; 1 bus per 50 workers
1 car per 1000 sqm.; 1 bus per 100 workers
questions.n: Industrial buildings like breweries require 1 car slot per 1000 sqm and 1 bus slot per 100 workers.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Mercantile Buildings like factories,
o: 1 car per 1000 sqm.; 1 bus per 100 workers
1 car per 100 sqm.; 1 bus per 100 workers
1 car per 500 sqm.; 1 bus per 100 workers
1 car per 1000 sqm.; 1 bus per 50 workers
questions.n: Factories follow the industrial standard of 1 car per 1000 sqm and 1 bus per 100 workers.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Public theaters, Cinemas, Assembly Halls, Dance halls, Skating rinks.
questions.n: General public assembly buildings require 1 car or jeepney slot per 50 square meters.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Amusement Parks.
questions.n: Amusement parks are categorized under general assembly, requiring 1 slot per 50 sqm.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Clubhouses, Beach houses and the likes.
questions.n: Private clubhouses and beach houses require 1 car or jeepney slot per 100 square meters.

questions.q: Parking space requirements for Agricultural Buildings if located in urbanized area.
questions.n: Even in urban areas, agricultural buildings only need 1 slot per 1000 sqm of Gross Floor Area.

questions.q: Lots bounded on all sides with 1 RROW, and 50% Open Space
questions.n: Interior lots are located behind other lots and require 50% open space due to restricted access.

questions.q: Lots bounded on 3 sides with 1 side facing a street 20% Open Space.
questions.n: Inside lots are standard lots with one street frontage and 20% required open space.

questions.q: Percentage of Open Space for Corner Lots.
questions.n: Corner lots have two street frontages, reducing the required open space to 10%.

questions.q: Percentage of Open Space for Through Lots.
questions.n: Through lots (facing two streets) have the lowest open space requirement at 5%.

questions.q: Percentage of Open Space for Corner-Through Lots.
questions.n: Like through lots, corner-through lots only require 5% open space.

questions.q: Percentage of Open Space for End Lots.
questions.n: End lots have high open space requirements, ranging from 30% to 50%.

questions.q: The required Open Spaces left after deducting the Outermost Face of the Bldg.
questions.n: A yard is the area between the property line and the building's outermost face.

questions.q: Minimum Horizontal distance of court and yards (setback).
questions.n: The code mandates a 2-meter minimum horizontal distance for yards and courts.

questions.q: Minimum front setback for R1 residentials.
questions.n: For R-1 residential properties, the front setback must be at least 4.5 meters.

questions.q: Minimum Ceiling Height for Artificially Ventilated rooms on first storey.
questions.n: Ground floor rooms with AC or fans must still be at least 2.70 meters high.

questions.q: Minimum Ceiling Height for Artificially Ventilated rooms on succeeding upper storeys.
questions.n: Upper floor rooms with artificial ventilation can have a reduced height of 2.40 meters.

questions.q: Minimum Ceiling Height for Naturally Ventilated rooms.
questions.n: Rooms without AC must have a minimum ceiling height of 2.70 meters regardless of the floor.

questions.q: Minimum height of Mezzanine floors.
questions.n: Mezzanine floors must have a clear height of at least 1.80 meters.

questions.q: Minimum Area of Rooms for Habitation.
questions.n: Any room used for habitation must have a minimum area of 6 square meters.

questions.q: Minimum Dimension of Rooms for Habitation.
questions.n: The shortest side of a habitable room must be at least 2.00 meters.

questions.q: Minimum area for Kitchen.
questions.n: A kitchen must have a minimum area of 3 square meters.

questions.q: Minimum Dimension for Kitchen.
questions.n: Kitchens must have a minimum horizontal dimension of 1.50 meters.

questions.q: Minimum Area of Toilet and Bath.
questions.n: The smallest allowable area for a toilet and bath is 1.20 square meters.

questions.q: Minimum Dimension for Toilet and Bath.
questions.n: The minimum width or length for a toilet and bath is 0.90 meters.

questions.q: Minimum Window openings as related to floor area for Rooms not provided with artificial Ventilation.
questions.n: Naturally ventilated rooms must have window openings equal to at least 10% of their floor area.

questions.q: Minimum Window openings as related to floor area for Toilet.
questions.n: Toilets require a smaller ratio of 1/20 (5%) of the floor area, or a fixed minimum of 240 sq. mm.

questions.q: Minimum clearance of window openings, eaves or canopies to side and rear property lines.
questions.n: Openings and eaves must maintain a minimum 750mm distance from side and rear property lines.

questions.q: Minimum width and height for Window openings intended to be used as emergency exits.
questions.n: Emergency exit windows must be at least 820mm wide and 1000mm high to allow a person to pass through.

questions.q: Minimum bottom openings for Windows intended to be used as emergency exits.
questions.n: The clear opening at the bottom of an emergency exit window must be at least 820mm.

questions.q: Minimum area of Vents Shafts.
questions.n: A vent shaft must have a minimum cross-sectional area of 1 square meter.

questions.q: Minimum dimension of Vents Shafts.
questions.n: The minimum horizontal dimension of a vent shaft is 600mm.

questions.q: Minimum unobstructed area of Air Ducts.
questions.n: Air ducts must maintain an unobstructed cross-sectional area of at least 0.30 square meters.
